topics.topic: Whether an owner request admitted before sign-out completes if sign-out acquires the session lock first
questions: If a request passes the session check before sign-out but sign-out acquires the session lock first, must the admitted request complete or be refused?
If a request passes the owner-session check before sign-out but acquires the session lock after sign-out, does it complete or get refused?

quotes: A request that passes completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs.
a change that takes the lock after the sign-out finds the session ended and is refused at the session check
judgement.why: The two passages give opposite outcomes for an already-admitted request when sign-out obtains the session lock first.

witness.initial: A valid owner session and a project whose correction form carries the current revision and CSRF value.
events: The owner submits the correction; it passes the owner-session and CSRF checks but pauses before acquiring the session lock.
The owner submits sign-out, which acquires the session lock and ends the session.
The correction then acquires the session lock.
outcomes: The admitted correction completes, changes the project and writes its audit entry.
The correction finds the session ended, is refused and changes nothing.
witness.observer: The owner sees after signing in again whether the corrected project and audit entry exist.
basis: The owner creates a project in the owner interface, corrects it, or adds a room to it; Cabinet Kernel adds a room for the agent on a project its session is granted (A09 rule 2).
The owner opens the owner interface and signs in with the owner credential; then makes requests in the session, signs out, or leaves it to expire.

A change then takes the session's one lock and holds it until done, so the session's changes apply one at a time; one that reads or changes an uploaded file takes the instance's import lock first (A16 rule 2).

topics.topic: Whether migration/import closure refusal precedes session, CSRF, and confirmation checks
questions: When an import closure exists, does the closure refusal preempt session, CSRF and confirmation processing, or is it checked only after those stage-(1) checks and their runtime effects?
When the migration closure exists but the submitted confirmation is absent, expired, already used, or wrong, is the request refused first for confirmation at stage (1), or for the closure?

quotes: A confirmation refused because the closure exists — made by any import accepted before it, of another session or of this one: nothing applied, every upload already dropped, and the import refused for good; no step is shown again (rule 8). This outcome comes before every other.

Under the import lock and the session's lock, `capability:owner_sessions.take_confirmation` uses the value up; `capability:store.run_in_transaction` opens the transaction with the action's instant from `capability:clock.recorded_now`; and `capability:migration_import.confirm_import` refuses when the closure exists or the file of the bound digest is no longer kept, checks the picks again (rule 6) and has each record written by its own module with its source identities and instants: `capability:projects.write_imported_project` the projects with their objects and rooms, `capability:customers.make_imported_customer` each Customer with a minted `customer_ref` at the action's instant, the v1 value moved to its tax id when the owner said so (R0-80), `capability:artifact_pointers.write_imported_pointer` the pointers, with the import as their publisher (M05).
judgement.why: One passage makes closure the first refusal, while the ordered step processes confirmation before the closure check.

bases.passage: A confirmation refused because the closure exists — made by any import accepted before it, of another session or of this one: nothing applied, every upload already dropped, and the import refused for good; no step is shown again (rule 8). This outcome comes before every other.

Under the import lock and the session's lock, `capability:owner_sessions.take_confirmation` uses the value up; `capability:store.run_in_transaction` opens the transaction with the action's instant from `capability:clock.recorded_now`; and `capability:migration_import.confirm_import` refuses when the closure exists or the file of the bound digest is no longer kept, checks the picks again (rule 6) and has each record written by its own module with its source identities and instants: `capability:projects.write_imported_project` the projects with their objects and rooms, `capability:customers.make_imported_customer` each Customer with a minted `customer_ref` at the action's instant, the v1 value moved to its tax id when the owner said so (R0-80), `capability:artifact_pointers.write_imported_pointer` the pointers, with the import as their publisher (M05).
bases.rests_on: A submission carries it when it passes the owner session and CSRF checks (A04 rule 6, stage 1) and gives a value equal to the pending one; from there on, whatever the answer — a binding to another action or input included — the pending value is used up.

unsupported_sides: A confirmation refused because the closure exists — made by any import accepted before it, of another session or of this one: nothing applied, every upload already dropped, and the import refused for good; no step is shown again (rule 8). This outcome comes before every other.

witness.initial: Owner session A has an uploaded import file and a valid pending confirmation value; owner session B then accepts an import, creates the closure and drops every session's upload.
events: Session A submits its old import form with a different confirmation value while its pending value remains valid.
outcomes: The confirmation check refuses the different value and leaves the pending confirmation unchanged without reaching the closure check.
The closure is checked first and the request is refused because the import is permanently closed.
witness.observer: The owner sees which refusal is returned, and session A retains or does not exercise its pending-confirmation state accordingly.
basis: Only when the mapping shows no malformed record, no conflict and no missing value (rule 1), `capability:owner_sessions.show_confirmation_step` binds a confirmation value to the import and the digest of the file's digest and the picks, names, aliases and Customer values (A13 rule 6).
An accepted import: the picked projects under their own ids with rooms, pointers and links, the Customers made, the closure and one entry; every session's upload dropped; every later import refused.
A submission refused before those checks, or giving another value while the pending one is still valid, is refused and leaves it as it was.
